title: Jacobs selected as key supply partner for Anglian Water’s Major Projects Framework
summary: Jacobs has been selected as a key supply partner for the VolkerFitzpatrick and VolkerStevin joint venture, which has secured a place on Anglian Water’s Major Projects Framework for Asset Management Periods 8 and 9.
body_markdown:
DALLAS –


[Jacobs](http://www.jacobs.com/) (NYSE: J) has been selected as a key supply partner for


the VolkerFitzpatrick and VolkerStevin joint venture, which has secured a place on Anglian Water’s Major Projects Framework


for Asset Management Periods 8 and 9 (AMP8/9).


Anglian Water estimates the 10-year framework at $2 billion (£1.5 billion), which will be spread across two contracts. It will provide capacity for major water and wastewater projects across the region, with initial work including coastal water quality improvements.


The framework’s initial work is organized into two portfolios. Green-First Urban projects will use sustainable drainage systems (SuDS) and green infrastructure to reduce storm overflow spills, support flood resilience and improve public spaces. Coastal Waters Quality Improvement projects will combine stormwater storage, overflow reductions and wastewater treatment upgrades to improve water quality at bathing and shellfish waters.


The Jacobs, VolkerFitzpatrick and VolkerStevin team will bring together process, civil, mechanical, electrical and control systems, and SuDS capabilities. Expected scope includes early contractor involvement, detailed design, construction and commissioning. The wider framework is anticipated to support additional major investments toward the end of AMP8 and through AMP9, as program needs develop.


**Jacobs Executive Vice President Richard Sanderson said** : “


We've built a strong track record with VolkerStevin and VolkerFitzpatrick over several years, and that experience is central to how we'll approach this framework. Leading our work from our Peterborough office keeps us close to local priorities and we look forward to bringing


the right technical disciplines around each project to improve water quality and strengthen resilience across the region.”


**VolkerWessels U.K. Board Director James Hindes said: “** Securing a place on this framework is a fantastic opportunity for our team and further strengthens our relationship with Jacobs. By combining our experience and expertise, we look forward to working collaboratively with Anglian Water to deliver important infrastructure that will improve water quality and strengthen resilience for communities across the region.”
